rationale.ai-code-insecurity: AI-assisted participants produced significantly more security-vulnerable code across four tasks.
rationale.automation-bias: Capable programmers trusted insecure AI outputs and overestimated solution security.
rationale.assistive: Users prompted, copied, edited, and accepted suggestion-level code during programming.
rationale.steering: Prompt strategies and parameter adjustments substantively shaped generated code security.
rationale.risk-security: Controlled tasks measured security flaws including injection, cryptography, and overflow vulnerabilities.
rationale.risk-overreliance: Acceptance behavior and confidence findings directly characterize over-reliance on AI.
rationale.method-self-report: Post-task surveys and participant comments measured trust and perceived security.
rationale.method-experiment: Participants were randomly assigned AI access during controlled programming tasks.
